description: Hi, I’m ND! I’d like to build a team where we can share ideas, learn from each other, and create something useful. I’m looking for motivated teammates with skills in [skills needed] who communicate openly and enjoy solving problems together. If that sounds like you, let’s team up!
summary: VegTwin Johor is a web prototype that helps small vegetable farms in Johor plan their next crop under climate risk. The user sets a field location on a map. The app reads a one-year NASA POWER climate snapshot for those coordinates, covering temperature, rainfall, humidity, heat stress and monsoon pressure. It then compares five crops (Sawi, Bayam, long beans, okra and cucumber) in a typical year, a monsoon season and a hot spell. Each crop gets an illustrative fit score, cycle length and field note. The tool is a planning aid to start a talk between a farmer and a field technician. It is not a weather forecast, and scores are not scientifically validated.
details:
• It locates a plot, senses the NASA POWER climate snapshot, and shifts the crop comparison across three views.
  • It uses the NASA POWER Daily API, OpenStreetMap through Leaflet, and a browser front end.
  • It is creative because the same location is stress-tested under monsoon and hot-spell views, and the ranking changes.
  • It has a commercial path through cooperatives and extension programmes (a hypothesis only), and it needs validation by agronomists.
